mount-buffalo-national-park-1.name: The Horn
mount-buffalo-national-park-1.bio: Highest point in Mount Buffalo National Park at 1,723 m, reached by a walk up from The Horn picnic area.

mount-buffalo-national-park-2.name: The Gorge (Mount Buffalo)
mount-buffalo-national-park-2.bio: Viewing area over the gorge near Mount Buffalo Chalet, where visitors watch the sunrise above valley fog.

mount-buffalo-national-park-3.name: The Cathedral (Mount Buffalo)
mount-buffalo-national-park-3.bio: Granite formation in Mount Buffalo National Park, reached from Cathedral Saddle and walked on the Cathedral - Hump track.

mount-buffalo-national-park-4.name: Eurobin Falls
mount-buffalo-national-park-4.bio: Waterfall in Mount Buffalo National Park on the Eurobin Falls Walk, fullest after rain and ringed by spring wildflowers.

mount-buffalo-national-park-5.name: Lake Catani
mount-buffalo-national-park-5.bio: Alpine lake in Mount Buffalo National Park, dammed in 1910, with a swimming spot, shoreline campground and wombats.

mount-buffalo-national-park-6.name: Mount Buffalo Chalet
mount-buffalo-national-park-6.bio: Heritage-listed 1910 timber chalet, the Alps' first ski resort; the exterior and terraced gardens are open to visit.

alpine-national-park-1.name: Bogong High Plains
alpine-national-park-1.bio: Alpine plateau reached from Falls Creek and Hotham, used for summer bushwalking and winter cross-country skiing.

alpine-national-park-2.name: Mount Bogong
alpine-national-park-2.bio: Victoria's highest mountain at 1,986 m, with an exposed summit ridge and emergency shelters on the Staircase Spur.

alpine-national-park-3.name: Mount Hotham
alpine-national-park-3.bio: Ski resort village in the Victorian Alps with a summer tracks network, guided walks and the Razorback.

alpine-national-park-4.name: Falls Creek
alpine-national-park-4.bio: Alpine village on the Bogong High Plains with summer mountain biking, hiking and a village museum.

alpine-national-park-5.name: Mount Feathertop
alpine-national-park-5.bio: Victoria's second-highest peak at 1,922 m, with snow in its summit gullies until late spring and exposed routes.

alpine-national-park-6.name: Falls to Hotham Alpine Crossing
alpine-national-park-6.bio: A 37 km, three-day hike from Falls Creek to Mt Hotham past historic huts, with a permit needed to camp.

alpine-national-park-7.name: The Razorback
alpine-national-park-7.bio: Exposed, relatively flat 11 km ridge from Diamantina Hut near Mt Hotham to the summit of Mount Feathertop.

mansfield-1.name: Mount Buller
mansfield-1.bio: Alpine resort with 85 ski trails in winter and a sightseeing chairlift, hiking, biking and a via ferrata in summer.

mansfield-2.name: Mount Stirling
mansfield-2.bio: Alpine resort with about 60 km of cross-country trails, plus a summit loop walk and year-round camping.

mansfield-3.name: Lake Eildon
mansfield-3.bio: Large reservoir on the Goulburn River for sailing, fishing and houseboats, with lookouts over the lake.

mansfield-4.name: Craig's Hut Walk
mansfield-4.bio: Short walk on Mount Stirling to the 1982 hut built as the set for The Man from Snowy River.

mansfield-5.name: Mount Howitt Walking Track
mansfield-5.bio: A 14 km return walk to the 1,742 m summit through snow gum forest, passing the hut at Macalister Springs.

mansfield-6.name: Lake Eildon National Park
mansfield-6.bio: National park around Lake Eildon with swimming, sailing and fishing, plus Merlo Lookout and the Blowhard Summit walk.

mansfield-7.name: Mount Samaria State Park
mansfield-7.bio: Semi-remote state park with 360-degree summit views, Wild Dog Falls, 1920s logging kilns and free camping.

mansfield-8.name: Lake Nillahcootie
mansfield-8.bio: Reservoir behind a 1967 dam, popular for water-skiing in summer, with a boat ramp and coffee van at the north end.

mansfield-9.name: Mansfield Zoo
mansfield-9.bio: Zoo on 30 acres where visitors hand-feed deer, kangaroos and emus, with white lions and meerkats.

bright-1.name: Harrietville
bright-1.bio: Village at the head of the Ovens Valley with walking tracks, including the Tronoh Dredge circuit.

bright-2.name: Wandiligong
bright-2.bio: Small village about 6 km south of Bright, reached as a short side trip from the town.

bright-3.name: Tronoh Dredge Walking Track
bright-3.bio: A 1.4 km, 30-minute loop around the dredge hole left by one of the world's largest electric dredges (1942-54).

bright-4.name: Mount Beauty Gorge Walk
bright-4.bio: A 1 km walk to a swing bridge over the West Kiewa River, then a swimming hole and a 1950s hydro adit.

beechworth-1.name: Old Beechworth Gaol
beechworth-1.bio: Granite gaol completed in 1864 that held Ned Kelly, now open for 45-minute guided tours daily.

beechworth-2.name: Yackandandah
beechworth-2.bio: National Trust-classified gold town with original shopfronts and a 37-site self-guided High Street heritage walk.

beechworth-3.name: Chiltern
beechworth-3.bio: Gold-rush town with a preserved main street and National Trust Dow's Pharmacy, a chemist from 1859 to 1968.

beechworth-4.name: Lake Sambell
beechworth-4.bio: Lake and parkland in Beechworth with a 2 km circuit and a bird hide, linked by a walk to Lake Kerferd.

beechworth-5.name: Chiltern-Mount Pilot National Park
beechworth-5.bio: Eucalypt forest park with a short walk to Mount Pilot Lookout's 360-degree views and the 8.5 km Whitebox track.

beechworth-6.name: Eldorado Dredge
beechworth-6.bio: 1930s steel gold dredge with 110 buckets that dug 30 million cubic metres from the Eldorado Plain.

beechworth-7.name: Yackandandah Gorge Scenic Walk
beechworth-7.bio: Walk along a gold-rush sluicing gorge beside a creek with small waterfalls, steep at the top.

wangaratta-1.name: Glenrowan
wangaratta-1.bio: Town where Ned Kelly's gang made their last stand in 1880, with an animated theatre, a museum and Big Ned.

wangaratta-2.name: Milawa
wangaratta-2.bio: King Valley village at the heart of Australia's first official gourmet region, with Brown Brothers and Milawa Cheese.

wangaratta-3.name: King Valley
wangaratta-3.bio: King River wine valley where 1940s-50s Italian migrants turned from tobacco to sangiovese, nebbiolo and barbera.

wangaratta-4.name: Warby-Ovens National Park
wangaratta-4.bio: Park 10 km from Wangaratta with river red gum forest, the granite Warby Range, lookouts and spring wildflowers.

wangaratta-5.name: The Big Ned Kelly
wangaratta-5.bio: Large statue of Ned Kelly on the Glenrowan roadside, in the Wangaratta area.

wangaratta-6.name: Kellyland Glenrowan
wangaratta-6.bio: Animated re-enactment of the Kelly Gang's last stand at Glenrowan, with a museum of wanted posters and Ned's death mask.

wangaratta-7.name: Ned Kelly Museum
wangaratta-7.bio: Glenrowan museum of Kelly relics beside a homestead, set in Kate's Cottage on Gladstone Street.

tallangatta.name: Tallangatta
tallangatta.bio: Lake Hume town moved 8 km west in the 1950s to make way for the expanded lake, as its entry sign says.

paradise-falls-cheshunt.name: Paradise Falls (Cheshunt)
paradise-falls-cheshunt.bio: Alpine National Park waterfall about 20 minutes from Whitfield, reached by a 500 m walk and best after rain.

lake-william-hovell.name: Lake William Hovell
lake-william-hovell.bio: Reservoir at the top of the King River valley with a swimming area, foreshore picnics, canoeing and a shoreline walk.

dartmouth-dam.name: Dartmouth Dam
dartmouth-dam.bio: A 180 m dam across the Mitta Mitta River, Victoria's largest by capacity, with a picnic area, boat ramp and fishing.

australian-alps-walking-track.name: Australian Alps Walking Track
australian-alps-walking-track.bio: About 650 km ridge and high-plains track from Walhalla to Tharwa, often walked in sections like the Bogong High Plains.

murray-to-the-mountains-rail-trail.name: Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail
murray-to-the-mountains-rail-trail.bio: Sealed off-road trail of about 95 km from Wangaratta to Bright on the old railway line, with a branch to Beechworth.

omeo.name: Omeo
omeo.bio: Alps town on the Great Alpine Road where gold was found in 1845, with the 1893 court house and Oriental Claims diggings.

omeo-mountain-bike-park.name: Omeo Mountain Bike Park
omeo-mountain-bike-park.bio: 114 km of mountain bike trails near Omeo, from easy Livingstone Creek greens to double-black descents of up to 590 m.

corryong.name: Corryong
corryong.bio: Upper Murray town promoted as the setting of The Man from Snowy River, with Jack Riley's grave in its cemetery.

burrowa-pine-mountain-national-park.name: Burrowa-Pine Mountain National Park
burrowa-pine-mountain-national-park.bio: National park in the upper Murray near Cudgewa and Tintaldra, managed by Parks Victoria.

mount-lawson-state-park.name: Mount Lawson State Park
mount-lawson-state-park.bio: State park 70 km east of Albury-Wodonga with walks to lookouts, waterfalls and rocky creeks, via an unsealed road.
